decisions.reason: The necessary cross-Requirement effect is already fully represented by the candidate's message-154 MODIFY, which requires the E and L to follow the Hero V's entire architectural vocabulary as members of the same proprietary alphabet.

The source Event's expansion of the Hero V's architectural-vocabulary role does not alter the second V's height hierarchy; the separate second-V clarification in the same message already has its own MODIFY.
The accent's existing requirement for literal derivation from the exact Hero V terminal remains valid unchanged; expanding the Hero V's vocabulary role adds no necessary derivation update.
The second V is already required to be a proprietary form engineered from the approved Hero V's shared geometry and gesture, so the source decision introduces no necessary construction-state change.
The candidate already has a message-154 MODIFY recording architectural E and L construction as a locked member of the Hero V-defined proprietary alphabet; no augmentation or removal is required.
Defining the Hero V as the source of the full architectural vocabulary does not change the existing exact peak-alignment rule or its fixed-reference method.
The source decision governs the proprietary construction language of the letters, not the wordmark's kerning or cohesive-reading goal.
The Hero V's expanded architectural role does not change the deferred champagne-metal material direction, role, or application constraint.
The source decision does not change the selected all-caps case treatment or its status as the preferred initial direction.
Review-image delivery formats are unrelated to the Hero V's architectural vocabulary and remain valid unchanged.
